paragraph: Burundi's national data governance strategy was [validated at a workshop in Bujumbura on 7 November 2025, with more than 60 delegates](<https://www.uneca.org/stories/burundi-validates-national-data-governance-strategy>). [The UN Economic Commission for Africa co-led the work](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/burundi-adopts-national-data-governance-strategy>), and [the ceremony was chaired by the Ministry of Finance and Digital Economy](<https://www.digitalbusiness.africa/burundi-la-strategie-nationale-de-gouvernance-des-donnees-devoilee/>). [A national data governance committee and an action plan for 2026 to 2028 are listed as next steps, not yet in place](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/burundi-validates-its-first-national-data-governance-strategy>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the government has approved or launched the strategy. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Botswana has a national data strategy being drafted. [The Ministry of Communications and Innovation held five days of training and stakeholder engagement from 7 to 11 September 2026 to support its development, with African Union Commission and European Union support](<https://dig.watch/updates/botswana-national-data-strategy-engagement>). In the last twelve months, this is the only step found, and no earlier position is dated. The same source mentions an earlier national data policy and does not say it was adopted. No source found says the government has approved or launched the strategy, or names a body to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Côte d'Ivoire's national data governance strategy to 2030 was [presented on 13 March 2025, after eight months of preparation, and handed to the Prime Minister for adoption](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/cote-divoire-unveils-ai-and-data-governance-strategy>). [The strategy's own text carries the Prime Minister's foreword on its official launch by the government](<https://www.telecom.gouv.ci/new/uploads/publications/174196707541.pdf>), and the text gives no launch date. The March 2025 presentation named a national committee for AI and data governance as a first action still to be created. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a council, office, agency or committee set up to carry out the strategy. Operating would need a body named to carry out the policy.

DR Congo's six-pillar national data governance strategy was [validated at a ceremony in Kinshasa on 13 November 2025 and handed over to the government, with amendments still being taken in](<https://www.uneca.org/stories/eca-officially-hands-over-the-national-data-governance-strategy-to-the-government-of-the-drc>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the government has approved or launched it. No source found names a body set up to carry it out. None names a rule issued under it. Establishing would need the government to adopt the strategy, approved by cabinet or launched or issued by the head of state, the minister or the responsible agency.

Congo has a national data governance strategy being drafted. [The UN Economic Commission for Africa supported consultations in Brazzaville from 2 to 9 June 2026](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/5882/eca-supports-republic-of-the-congo-in-developing-national-data-governance-strategy>), [after a self-assessment found the country had no integrated strategy](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/eca-supporting-republic-congo-shaping-national-data-governance-strategy-digital-sovereignty-and>). [A workshop of 60 participants on 8 and 9 June 2026 followed an assessment that consulted 21 institutions](<https://www.uneca.org/fr/stories/la-r%C3%A9publique-du-congo-veut-%C3%A9tablir-les-fondements-d%E2%80%99un-%C3%A9cosyst%C3%A8me-de-donn%C3%A9es-fiable>). In the last twelve months, these consultations are the steps found. No source found says the government has approved or launched the strategy. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

The Comoros has a national data governance strategy for 2027 to 2031. [Government, private-sector and civil-society representatives met in Moroni on 24 and 25 August 2026 to review and validate it, with its implementation plan](<https://www.nepad.org/news/lauda-nepad-sassocie-lunion-des-comores-pour-impulser-la-transformation-numerique>). [On 21 October 2026 the telecommunications minister presented the strategy to the Council of Ministers](<https://alwatwan.net/politique/conseil-des-ministres-i-approbation-d%E2%80%99un-projet-d%E2%80%99%C3%A9lectrification-compl%C3%A8te-de-la-r%C3%A9gion-de-mledjele-%C3%A0-mwali.html>). In the last twelve months, these two steps are the ones found, and no earlier position is dated. No source found says the Council of Ministers approved the strategy, or names a body to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Cabo Verde's National Statistics Council [held a conference in Praia on 24 and 25 April 2025 on the country's first national data strategy](<https://www.mf.gov.cv/web/mf/-/conselho-nacional-de-estat%C3%ADstica-promove-confer%C3%AAncia-para-discutir-a-estrat%C3%A9gia-nacional-de-dados>). In the last twelve months, [senior officials, the Secretary of State for the Digital Economy, consultants and European Union representatives held a kick-off meeting on 28 April 2026 on a Data Strategy for Public Administration](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/05/04/cape-verde-launches-national-data-and-ai-strategies-to-modernize-public-administration/>). No source found says the government has approved a strategy. None names a body to carry one out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Algeria's national data governance framework was set up by [Presidential Decree 25-320 of 30 December 2025, with a data classification reference, a data cataloguing reference and a national interoperability system](<https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/JO-FRANCAIS/2025/F2025087.pdf>). [The Prime Minister presided over its official launch on 9 February 2026](<https://www.maghrebinfo.dz/2026/02/09/un-socle-fondamental-pour-ledification-dun-etat-moderne-apte-a-anticiper-les-defis-futurs/>), and [the High Commissioner for Digitalisation installed a national commission of all ministries and national bodies to follow its implementation](<https://www.maghrebinfo.dz/2026/02/09/un-socle-fondamental-pour-ledification-dun-etat-moderne-apte-a-anticiper-les-defis-futurs/>). In the last twelve months, the framework was set up and launched. In February 2026, [every ministry had been written to to start classifying its data](<https://almostathmir.dz/%D8%AD%D9%88%D9%83%D9%85%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A8%D9%8A%D8%A7%D9%86%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D9%81%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AC%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%B1-%D8%AA%D8%B9%D8%B2%D9%8A%D8%B2-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A7/>). No source found gives the date or text of the decision issuing the two references. None says how many ministries have classified their data.

Ethiopia has a national data governance strategy and a law in draft. [Work on the strategy began under the Office of the Prime Minister, with a technical committee](<https://dial.global/lessons-from-ethiopias-data-strategy-approach/>), and [its draft framework was expanded into a full draft strategy](<https://dial.global/lessons-from-ethiopias-data-strategy-approach/>). In the last twelve months, [the strategy was described as forthcoming in March 2026](<https://dial.global/ethiopias-approach-to-use-cases/>). [On 28 September 2026 the Council of Ministers referred the National Data Governance Draft Proclamation to the House of Peoples' Representatives](<https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_9629721>). No source found says the strategy has been launched or the bill enacted. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Ghana has a national data strategy in draft. [On 2 July 2024 the government, the European Union and Smart Africa completed a two-day national validation workshop on the draft and its implementation roadmap](<https://smartafrica.org/ghana-develops-its-national-data-strategy-in-collaboration-with-smart-africa-and-team-europe>). No change has been found in the last twelve months, and nothing newer on the strategy has been found. No source found says the government has approved or launched it, or names a body set up to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Guinea has a national data governance strategy being written. [The government launched the drafting on 19 June 2026, led by the National Directorate of Information Technology and the Digital Economy](<https://www.ecofinagency.com/news/2606-56858-guinea-begins-work-on-national-data-governance-strategy>). [The minister opened the stakeholder workshop that day](<https://mceni.gov.gn/la-guinee-engage-lelaboration-de-sa-strategie-nationale-de-gouvernance-des-donnees/>), [after an assessment mission in Conakry from 16 to 19 June that consulted 27 institutions](<https://www.uneca.org/stories/guinea-lays-the-foundations-for-a-trusted-and-inclusive-national-data-governance-framework>). In the last twelve months, these are the only steps found, and no earlier position is dated. No source found says a draft exists or that the government has approved or launched it. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

The Gambia has a national data policy in draft. [On 2 and 3 July 2025 stakeholders from government, the private sector, civil society and academia endorsed it at a national validation workshop, and the European Union delegation said the finalised policy would be submitted for government approval](<https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/gambia/gambia-moves-closer-stronger-data-governance-validating-its-national-data-policy-validated_en>). The Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy's [draft National Data Policy 2025](<https://mocde.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/National-Data-Policy-2025-The-Gambia-draft.docx>) is held. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says the government has approved or launched it. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Guinea-Bissau's Council of Ministers, chaired by the Prime Minister, [approved the draft decree on a national data governance and protection policy](<https://ang.gw/governo-aprova-projeto-de-regulamento-sobre-a-interoperabilidade-de-sistemas-e-plataformas-digitais/>). The state news agency reported this on 10 July 2025 and gave no date for the meeting other than the day of the week. No text of the policy has been found. No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a council, office, agency, committee, chief data officer or ministry unit set up or named to carry it out. Operating would need a body named to carry out the policy.

Kenya has a national data governance policy in draft. [Drafting began at a workshop in September 2025, with support from the EU and GIZ](<https://www.kenyanews.go.ke/national-data-governance-policy-formulation-kicks-off/>). In the last twelve months, [the ICT ministry held a validation workshop for the public sector on 5 February 2026, with the draft then to be finalised, approved by cabinet and launched](<https://www.ict.go.ke/government-moves-strengthen-kenyas-data-governance-framework>). [A final draft is dated 25 May 2026](<https://rosemutiso.substack.com/p/kenya-wants-to-sell-your-data-but>), and [in August 2026 it was still described as being developed](<https://cipit.strathmore.edu/the-standing-cabinet-committee-on-artificial-intelligence-implications-for-kenyas-evolving-ai-ecosystem/>). No source found says cabinet has approved it, or names a body set up to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Liberia has a national data governance policy in draft. [The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, with the African Union Commission, held a consultation in Monrovia on 13 and 14 November 2025 to prepare it](<https://www.thenewdawnliberia.com/liberia-moves-to-strengthen-data-governance-under-au-led-initiative/>). In the last twelve months, [the policy text of March 2026 is marked draft and says it will be published upon approval](<https://mopt.gov.lr/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/2026-Liberia-Data-Governance-Policy-REVISED-CIPESA-1.pdf>). No source found says the government has approved or launched it, or names a body set up to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Libya has a national guide for government data governance in use. [The General Information Authority reported on 23 April 2026 that it applies the guide](<https://www.gia.gov.ly/en/2026/04/23/the-general-information-authority-strengthens-data-governance-at-the-libyan-zakat-fund-according-to-the-national-guide-for-government-data-governance/>), which is its reference framework for how government bodies manage data, keep it accurate and share it. In the last twelve months, this report is the only dated step found. The authority that applies the guide is the one responsible for government data in general. No source found gives the date the guide was issued, or its text, or names a council, office, committee or unit set up to carry it out. Operating would need a body named to carry out the policy.

Lesotho's ICT minister [signed the government's Data Management Policy in Maseru on 11 June 2026](<https://lestimes.com/?p=90715>). [A validation workshop on 13 October 2025 had aligned the draft with the African Union's Data Policy Framework](<https://www.gov.ls/government/follow-up-on-lesotho-data-governance-capacity-building-and-engagement-workshop/>). In the last twelve months, the draft validated in October 2025 was signed, and [in November 2026 the minister told an ITU conference that government had approved it](<https://www.gov.ls/development/lesotho-calls-for-affordable-international-connectivity-for-landlocked-countries-to-ensure-they-are-not-left-behind-in-the-digital-transformation-agenda/>). No source found names a body set up to carry out the policy, or a law, regulation, standard or guideline issued under it. Operating would need a body named to carry out the policy.

No stage is set. Nothing since March 2020 shows a national data policy being written in Morocco. A December 2024 article says none has been formalised, but not that none is being written. Also found are [Digital Morocco 2030](<https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/morocco-digital-economy>) and [a draft Digital X.0 framework law](<https://www.wearetech.africa/en/fils-uk/news/tech/morocco-drafts-landmark-law-to-govern-ai-data-and-digital-identity>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Absent would need a source from the past three years saying the country has no national data policy and none is being written.

Mozambique has a national data governance policy and strategy in draft. [A workshop in Maputo on 5 December 2025 validated the proposed policy, strategy and action plan](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/12/05/mozambique-prioritizes-data-governance-as-cornerstone-of-digital-sovereignty/>). In the last twelve months, the draft stayed unapproved. [The communications minister said on 22 July 2026 that they were still in preparation and not yet approved](<https://news.isocmedias.co.mz/2026/07/23/governo-prepara-lei-de-protecao-de-dados-pessoais/>). The information technology institute [said the same in August 2026](<https://itweb.africa/article/mozambique-steps-up-ai-drive/nWJadvbND3dvbjO1>). No source found names a body set up to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Mauritius has a National Data Strategy for 2025 to 2029. [The Ministry of Information Technology, Communication and Innovation, with the Data Protection Office, officially launched it at Ebene on 28 January 2026](<https://lexpress.mu/node/553938>). In the last twelve months, [the minister spoke on 16 July 2026 of the government carrying out a national data governance strategy](<https://mitci.govmu.org/mitci/mauritius-to-join-america-india-connect-subsea-cable-programme-announces-pm-ramgoolam/>). The Data Protection Office took part in the launch, and the source does not say that carrying out the strategy is its job. No source found names a council, office, agency, committee, chief data officer or ministry unit set up or named to carry it out. Operating would need a body named to carry out the policy.

[President Buhari launched the National Data Policy at the State House, Abuja, on 2 February 2023](<https://fmino.gov.ng/at-the-launch-of-two-policies-on-digital-economy-president-buhari-says-diversification-has-been-most-successful-in-the-sector/>). [On 19 July 2023 the Director-General of the National Information Technology Development Agency inaugurated a Technical Working Group for implementing the National Data Strategy](<https://leadership.ng/nitda-unveils-national-data-strategy-to-drive-nigerias-digital-economy/>), to recommend how regulatory agencies implement it. [The draft strategy's timetable lists a governance structure and a strategy implementation committee still to be established, for November and December 2022](<https://nitda.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2022/11/Final-Draft-National-Data-Strategy.pdf>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found names a law, regulation, standard or guideline issued under the policy. Mature would need a rule or standard issued under the policy.

Rwanda's cabinet [approved the National Data Sharing Policy on 26 May 2025; the ICT ministry developed it with the Rwanda Information Society Authority, for the exchange of data across public institutions](<https://www.risa.gov.rw/news-detail/national-data-sharing-policy-approved>). [A Data Governance Unit has been set up at the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda as the operational arm of the policy](<https://cenfri.org/articles/what-will-determine-the-success-of-rwandas-data-governance-push/>). In the last twelve months, a report of May 2026 said the unit has staff in place and projects started. No source found from the last three years names a law, regulation, standard or guideline issued under the policy. The seven annexes came with the policy itself. Mature would need a rule or standard issued under the policy.

Senegal's National Data Strategy was adopted by October 2024, when [Le Tech Observateur listed it among the authorities' recent strategies](<https://letechobservateur.sn/mise-a-niveau-du-projet-de-loi-sur-la-protection-des-donnees-personnelles-une-avancee-majeure-pour-le-cadre-legal-senegalais/>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: [a report of July 2026 also says the strategy is adopted](<https://lequotidien.sn/mbour-gouvernance-des-donnees-et-intelligence-artificielle-vers-un-nouveau-dispositif-normatif/>). [A separate national blueprint on creating value from data was validated on 21 and 22 September 2026](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/09/23/senegal-validates-national-blueprint-data-valorisation/>), with its roadmap and monitoring still to be refined. No body set up to carry out the strategy has been found. Operating would need a body named to carry out the policy.

Sierra Leone's [Ministry of Information and Communications published its first National Data Strategy in January 2023, and it carries no end date](<https://mocti.gov.sl/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Sierra-Leone-National-Data-Strategy_2023_v1.pdf>). [A five-month engagement in 2025 updated it to align with the African Union's Data Policy Framework](<https://dial.global/work/strengthening-national-data-strategy-sierra-leone>). In the last twelve months, [in August 2026 the ministry described training its technical team as part of carrying the strategy out](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/6855/sierra-leone-trains-government-technical-team-on-ai-and-data-protection-by-design>), and [in September 2026 it said it is developing a data governance framework](<https://sierraloaded.sl/news/communication-strengthens-partnership/>). No source found names a body set up to carry out the strategy. Operating would need a body named to carry out the policy.

[A GIZ African Union post of 13 March 2026 says Somalia validated a National Data Policy Framework under the AU-GIZ Data Governance in Africa Initiative](<https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7438141176852996097>). The framework covers collection, management, sharing, classification, retention and data sovereignty. The post gives no date for the validation. In the last twelve months, this post is the only step found, and no earlier position is dated. The post names no body set up to carry the framework out and no rule issued under it. No source found says the government has approved or launched it. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

In July 2025 the national innovation institute [published a first version of the design of the 2025 to 2030 data strategy and data governance policy](<https://inic.gov.st/viewdoc.php?id=27>), prepared by a consultant. It says no data governance policy yet exists and lists its approval as a future step. No change has been found in the last twelve months. The design document names no body yet given the job of carrying the policy out. No source found says the government has approved or launched it. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Eswatini has a national data governance policy for 2027 to 2031 in draft. [A first stakeholders' workshop opened in Mbabane on 29 April 2026, with European Union support](<https://www.eeas.europa.eu/delegations/eswatini/eu-proud-support-eswatini-developing-national-data-policy_en>). In the last twelve months, [the draft was reviewed and validated in July 2026](<https://techreviewafrica.com/news/6470/eswatini-validates-national-data-governance-policy>), and [the ICT minister told the Senate in August 2026 that it is expected to be completed before the end of 2026](<https://eswatinipositivenews.online/data-governance-policy-to-be-completed-by-year-end-minister-savannah/>). [In September 2026 iMedias reported that the policy had been prepared](<https://www.imedias.net/leswatini-adopte-sa-premiere-politique-de-gouvernance-des-donnees/>), and named no date of approval and no approving body. No source found names a body set up to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Chad's national data governance strategy is a validated draft. [A national workshop of 50 participants reviewed and validated the strategy on 7 October 2026](<https://www.uneca.org/stories/chad-validates-national-data-governance-strategy%2C-marking-a-key-milestone-in-its-digital>). [Opening it, the minister said working-group amendments go to plenary before the strategy is adopted](<https://mten.gouv.td/discours-de-haliki-choua-mahamat-sur-la-gouvernance-des-donnees/>). In the last twelve months, [consultations began in N'Djamena on 13 May 2026](<https://www.uneca.org/eca-events/fr/node/2449>), and [a workshop opened on 18 May to prepare the drafting](<https://www.lepaystchad.com/transition-numerique-le-tchad/>). No source found says the government has adopted or launched the strategy, or names a body to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Tunisia has a national strategy for the governance, opening and valorisation of public data, in draft. [OGP Tunisie reports a workshop on 26 March 2026 to present and discuss the final draft](<http://www.ogptunisie.gov.tn/?p=6651>). [The draft was prepared under government decree 2021-3](<http://www.ogptunisie.gov.tn/?p=6651>). In the last twelve months, these workshops are the only steps found, and no earlier position is dated. Neither workshop names a council, office or agency to carry the strategy out. No source found says the government has approved it. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

Tanzania has an electronic data governance strategy in draft. [Its preparation was expected to be complete by January 2026](<https://www.mwananchi.co.tz/mw/habari/kitaifa/tanzania-yajipanga-ukinara-ulinzi-wa-data-uchumi-wa-kidijitali-afrika-5173946>). In the last twelve months, [a national validation workshop was held in Dodoma on 12 March 2026, where the ministry's director reaffirmed the commitment to take it to formal adoption](<https://www.uneca.org/stories/the-blueprint-for-a-digital-sovereign-nation-tanzania-validates-its-landmark-electronic-data>). No source found says the government has approved or launched it, or names a body set up to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.

[The Minister of State for ICT and National Guidance launched the Uganda National Data Strategy in Kampala on 20 October 2026](<https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/science/uganda-launches-national-data-strategy-NV_242720_102026>). [The strategy provides for a National Data Steering Committee chaired by the finance ministry](<https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/science/uganda-launches-national-data-strategy-NV_242720_102026>), and a National Data Office within the ICT ministry is to coordinate delivery. In the last twelve months, the strategy went from [a first draft written at a workshop in Jinja in February 2024](<https://ict.go.ug/media/news/paving-the-way-for-a-data-driven-future-through-a-national-data-strategy>) to launch. [The Uganda Bureau of Statistics called the launch illegal and redundant the next day](<https://www.independent.co.ug/ubos-rejects-new-national-data-strategy-labels-ict-ministry-launch-illegal-and-redundant/>). No source found names a law, regulation, standard or guideline issued under the strategy. Mature would need a rule or standard issued under the policy.

South Africa's [National Policy on Data and Cloud, gazetted on 31 May 2024](<https://www.gov.za/sites/default/files/gcis_document/202406/50741gen2533.pdf>), sets government policy on collecting, storing, using and sharing data. [On 2 April 2025 the Minister for Public Service and Administration signed a directive on data governance](<https://www.dpsa.gov.za/dpsa2g/documents/km/2025/Determination%20and%20Directive%20on%20the%20Implementation%20of%20Data%20Governance%20in%20the%20Public%20Service.pdf>), in force on signature. It requires each head of a national or provincial department to set up a data governance committee and to appoint a chief data officer. No change has been found in the last twelve months, nor any report that departments have done so. Mature would need a rule or standard issued under the policy.

Zambia has a national data policy being drafted. [Research ICT Africa says it supported the drafting of the Zambian National Data Policy under its DataCipation project with GIZ and AUDA-NEPAD](<https://researchictafrica.net/project/datacipation-shaping-harmonised-and-inclusive-digital-and-data-policies-in-africa/>). The project page, from September 2026, gives no date for a finished draft. In the last twelve months, this page is the only step found, and no earlier position is dated. No source found says the government has validated, approved or launched the policy, or names a body set up to carry it out. Establishing would need the policy adopted by cabinet or launched by the head of state, minister or agency.
